territorial_scope.description: Applies within the City of Chandler, Arizona, through amendment of the city zoning code.

evidence.quote: Data Centers are not permitted to operate in the City of Chandler

summary.short: Amends Chandler City Code Chapter 35 to define data center and add Section 35-2214 regulating data centers. Data centers are not permitted unless approved in a Planned Area Development district or as limited ancillary uses, with neighbor notice, meetings, noise studies, and backup-generator notice duties. Adopted December 2022.
summary.long: Ordinance No. 5033 amends the City of Chandler, Arizona zoning code (Chapter 35) relating to data centers. Section 1 adds a definition of Data Center as a facility or portion of a facility housing networked computer systems and telecommunications equipment used for remote storage, processing, and distribution of data. Section 2 adds Section 35-2214. Data centers are not permitted to operate in the city unless explicitly approved as part of a Planned Area Development zoning district. Data centers ancillary to another primary use are permitted if they occupy no more than ten percent of the building footprint, serve the enterprise functions of the on-site property owner rather than leasing storage or processing to third parties, and are not in a separate stand-alone structure. Before a data center is built in a Planned Area Development district, the property owner must notify residents and homeowners associations within a half-mile radius by mail, and the operator must hold two neighborhood meetings with posted signs. A third-party acoustic engineer must document baseline sound levels before the first meeting, and the building must include sound mitigation so that emitted sound does not exceed baseline ambient levels. After occupancy, noise studies are required at completion and annually for five years, with results sent to the city. On request, the operator must provide an on-site neighborhood liaison from 8:00 am to 10:00 pm to respond to noise complaints. Backup generator testing and routine operation must be announced on a public website at least 24 hours in advance and notified to the city, generally limited to 9:00 am to 5:00 pm on weekdays except during outages. Sections 3 and 4 repeal conflicting ordinances and provide for severability. The ordinance was adopted by the City Council in December 2022.

notes: Day numbers in the scanned text are inconsistent: the introduction date reads 'this 5 ___ day of December' and the adoption date appears as a standalone '8'; publication is stated as December 16 and December 23, 2022. Sec. 35-2214(2)(b) cites Sec. 35-2601.1 (sign design standards) and the text cites an exhibit on file with the City Clerk; neither is included in this text. Sec. 35-2214(1) bars Data Centers unless approved in a Planned Area Development district, with an ancillary-use exception. Obligations are placed on the 'operator', the 'property owner', or both, without a stated distinction. Thresholds, enforcement and penalties are absent from the text.

enforcement.note: The ordinance sets operative conditions, including that Data Centers are not permitted to operate unless approved in a Planned Area Development district (Sec. 35-2214(1)), but the document states no fine, penalty, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension, blocking or injunction for non-compliance, and names no enforcement authority for such a sanction. The document contains no sanction provision and does not cross-reference one.
